text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
- On March 31 Norway will withdraw from the base at Rimini in Italy its NATO task force serving in the former Yugoslavia. The force has been there since December 1995.

- Norway's road haulage association says Germany discriminates against Norwegian transport companies in favour of operators from European Union members. Norway is not an EU member. Germany refuses to refund VAT on fuel to Norwegian drivers, while German vehicles in Norway are fully refunded.
- An enormous crater made by a meteorite in the Norwegian sector of the Barents Sea millions of years ago is believed to be one of the world's largest structures of its type.

- Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, Norway's second largest commercial bank, says it is not interested in making a bid for mortgage lender BNbank. That leaves the takeover battle between Den norske Bank and Fokus Bank.

- Pharmaceuticals company Nycomed claims its share price has been manipulated over the past week. Eric Cameron, head spokesman at Nycomed, says for two days in a row groundless rumours were planted in the market, which sent the share price down eight percent.

- National Planning Minister Bendik Rugaas has criticised Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg for reacting too hastily in tightening up the regulations governing the securities dealings for people working in the financial sector.
